notes: gopher64 (N64): upstream's bare linux-aarch64 executable -- no aarch64 N64 AppImage exists anywhere (plan gopher64). retroforge-emu saves it as <tag>.AppImage all the same; the binary format runs `current` in place, nothing to mount. SDL3 and wgpu are compiled in, Vulkan goes through the loader (the image's Turnip); the only shared libraries it needs (libc, libm, libgcc_s, libstdc++, libfontconfig) are in the rootfs.

--fullscreen sizes the window to the display; {rom} is the game (n64/v64/z64/bin, or a zip/7z holding one). No arguments is gopher64's own GUI: gui_args, for Main menu > Emulators > Open (upscaling and the other config.json settings live there).
SDL_NO_SIGNAL_HANDLERS: SDL3 catches SIGTERM, so OGUI's Exit would never end the emulator (the melonDS/Azahar lesson).

Saves and save states land in ~/.local/share/gopher64/{saves,states}, which user-tmpfiles (retroforge-home.conf) links to ~/saves/n64 and ~/states/n64; its settings are ~/.config/gopher64/config.json. The N64 needs no BIOS.

setup_args: gopher64 only reads a pad ASSIGNED to a port (a fresh config has none: no controls, HW 2026-10-20 Pocket ACE), and it stores the pad's /dev/input/eventN path, which no board or boot guarantees. --assign-controller 1 --port 1 before every start makes gopher64 itself write the current path of the first SDL joystick -- InputPlumber's virtual pad, the only one a RetroForge session shows.
